proofs.requirement: Recognition is one part of a therapeutic design; connected formats add separate actions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A recognition molecule can be used as one component of a larger therapeutic design. Its ability to bind is one property of that component.

proofs.semanticAssessment: The dedicated unmerged binder owner supplies the generic component definition; a modality record is not substituted for that owner.
proofs.sourceScope: Watson is a complete abstract about designed protein binders; Eshhar is a complete abstract about an experimental scFv receptor in a T-cell hybridoma. The generic component definition is a scoped synthesis, not a new clinical result.

proofs.requirement: The binder and the molecular target it contacts are distinct objects; purple and blue are drawing conventions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The antibody recognizes an accessible antigen; the attachment chemistry and linker affect stability and release; the payload acts through its own molecular mechanism.

proofs.semanticAssessment: Recognition and the recognized antigen are separate objects in the current ADC mechanism. The purple/blue labels remain a separately checked drawing choice.
proofs.sourceScope: The FDA ADC selected pages describe antibody/fragment, linker and payload in cytotoxic conjugates. They do not cover every therapeutic cargo. Purple and blue are authored identifiers, not molecular properties.

proofs.requirement: An accessible intended target can occur on cancer and healthy cells; recognition alone gives no tumour exclusivity or safety conclusion.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Healthy tissues can carry either recognized target

proofs.semanticAssessment: The current bispecific owner explicitly carries recognized targets on healthy tissue, with no safety conclusion from specificity alone.
proofs.sourceScope: The selected NCI paragraphs name CD20 on B cells and some cancer cells in its rituximab example. This supports possible shared recognition, not a statement that every cancer antigen is equally accessible on all healthy cells.

proofs.requirement: A binder need not be an entire antibody.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Primary antibody-fragment studies showed how recognition domains can be used outside a complete antibody.

proofs.semanticAssessment: The dedicated unmerged binder owner explicitly places recognition domains outside a complete antibody.
proofs.sourceScope: The Eshhar abstract uses an antibody scFv in an engineered surface receptor; the Watson abstract reports designed protein binders. Neither is evidence that every recognition scaffold has validated therapeutic function.

proofs.requirement: Linking chemical cargo to recognition does not by itself establish entry, processing or usable payload at its action site.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding can support delivery, but uptake, processing, access to the payload’s target and cellular response require separate evidence.

proofs.semanticAssessment: Binding, uptake, processing, action-site access and response remain separate.
proofs.sourceScope: FDA ADC printed pages 1 to 3 describe distinct constituent parts, release mechanisms and exposure considerations. The separate-test reading rule does not assume that every conjugate follows one guaranteed route.

proofs.requirement: Internalisation is not a universal requirement shared by all of the illustrated formats.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A change of format is a new product hypothesis. If an ADC binds M but yields little active material after uptake, an M-directed engager might avoid that particular processing requirement.

proofs.semanticAssessment: The current format-switching example explains how an engager can avoid a particular conjugate-processing requirement. This is a format-scope inference, not a claim that every construct works without uptake.
proofs.sourceScope: Mack describes one soluble CD3/17-1A single-chain construct redirecting human lymphocytes in cell experiments. Contrasting that mechanism with FDA cytotoxic-conjugate processing gives a format-scope inference; no universal uptake or benefit claim is made.

proofs.requirement: The illustrated soluble T-cell engager has distinct target-recognition and CD3-recognition arms binding different features on separate cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: CD20/CD3 lymphoma engagers illustrate one bispecific format: CD20 recognition connects to T-cell recruitment through CD3.
The Mack construct joined two single-chain Fv fragments with a peptide linker in one compact protein; this is different from an IgG architecture with an Fc region.

proofs.semanticAssessment: The named CD20/CD3 example and two linked scFv architecture jointly carry the illustrated distinct binding functions. Mack is one experimental construct, not a universal topology for every engager.
proofs.sourceScope: Mack describes two scFv fragments joined by a peptide linker, one directed at CD3 and the other at epithelial 17-1A. The NCI paragraph gives a separate named CD19/CD3 example. These are illustrative architectures, not all engager forms.

proofs.requirement: Bridging contact alone is not evidence of productive activation or target killing.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: T-cell engagers are proteins that bind a specified target and recruit T cells, often through CD3. A binding bridge does not by itself establish completed killing.

proofs.semanticAssessment: The registered engager TLDR explicitly withholds completed killing from a binding bridge.
proofs.sourceScope: Mack measured cytotoxicity separately from binding. Bluemel reports different lysis despite similar target affinity in engineered CHO systems. The no-guarantee reading rule is an inference about evidence, not a new failure frequency.

proofs.requirement: The cell-receptor example spans the T-cell membrane and links extracellular recognition to an intracellular signalling design.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region.

proofs.semanticAssessment: The registered CAR principle carries external recognition, transmembrane linkage and internal signalling.
proofs.sourceScope: Eshhar used anti-trinitrophenyl scFv linked to gamma or zeta signalling chains in a cytolytic T-cell hybridoma. The selected FDA CAR guidance concerns ex vivo manufactured products and separates recognition from signalling. Neither supplies a general clinical outcome.

proofs.requirement: A living-cell receptor and a soluble bridging protein are different formats; a floating antibody is not itself a cell receptor.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A dosed T-cell engager supplies a protein connecting target recognition to an available T cell. It does not itself install receptor instructions or supply engineered living responders.
The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects.

proofs.semanticAssessment: The protein engager and receptor-bearing living cell are explicitly different administered/design objects.
proofs.sourceScope: Mack concerns an expressed soluble bispecific protein; Eshhar concerns functional surface receptors in a cellular model. The FDA guidance discusses a living, genetically modified cell product. These object distinctions do not establish comparative efficacy.

proofs.requirement: Function of the assembled product needs testing; receptor anatomy or a signalling symbol is not a measured successful response.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding, surface CAR expression, activation, proliferation and completed target-cell killing are distinct readouts.
In this schematic sequence, simplified shapes and an arrow from recognition toward a response do not show that every cell expressed the receptor or completed killing.

proofs.semanticAssessment: Readouts and the schematic response arrow are explicitly separated from demonstrated expression or completed killing.
proofs.sourceScope: The FDA CAR construct section calls for supporting recognition and signalling functions and evaluating hinge/linker/transmembrane contributions. Eshhar measured IL2 secretion and lysis in a defined model. A drawn signalling ray is not one of these measurements.

proofs.requirement: Delivery, function, safety and patient benefit are distinct questions, without a binding-to-benefit progression.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Two specificities do not establish that both targets are reached together, that binding produces killing, or that a molecule improves on a comparison treatment. Function, exposure, manufacturing quality and harms need evidence for the actual product and indication. A class containing approved drugs does not make every bispecific design an approved therapy.
An antibody-drug conjugate links a target-binding antibody to an active drug. Binding, delivery, release and drug action each matter, and normal tissues can also be exposed.

proofs.semanticAssessment: Delivery, function, harms and comparative treatment evidence belong to the finished product; the binding result does not supply these unmeasured results.
proofs.sourceScope: FDA ADC selected pages keep constituent exposure and safety/efficacy questions separate. The selected CAR pages distinguish product characterisation, nonclinical assessment and clinical studies. The separate-question rule supplies no patient-benefit estimate.

proofs.requirement: A shared recognition idea does not prove identical module performance after reformatting; the complete product needs tests.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A change of format is a new product hypothesis. If an ADC binds M but yields little active material after uptake, an M-directed engager might avoid that particular processing requirement. It still needs its own binding and contact-geometry measurements, useful effector access and function, normal-tissue testing and clinical evidence. Earlier antibody or ADC tolerability does not establish the safety of a different action. Bystander delivery and two-address designs are possible responses to heterogeneous expression, not guaranteed coverage or an exhaustive list of solutions.
The full binder, spacer, anchor, signaling arrangement and cell preparation still matter.

proofs.semanticAssessment: A changed format is explicitly a new product hypothesis, with construct, geometry, expression and cell preparation retained.
proofs.sourceScope: Bluemel compared epitope distance and antigen size in transfected CHO cells and engineered surface targets, with different lysis despite similar affinity. The FDA CAR section says structural-region contributions should be evaluated. No format-wide ranking or guaranteed sequence portability follows.
